question: The huge storm known as Great red spot is associated with which planet?A. MarsB. VenusC. PlutoD. Jupiter (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: B
A
C
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jupiter

Explanation:
The Great Red Spot is a massive storm on Jupiter, larger than Earth. It is a high-pressure region that has been active for at least 350 years. It was first observed by Robert Hooke in 1664. The storm is composed of ammonia and water clouds in Jupiter's atmosphere. The exact reason for its red color is not fully understood, but it is believed to be due to chemical reactions with sunlight. Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system and is classified as a gas giant. It has a strong magnetic field and at least 95 known moons, including Ganymede, the largest moon in the solar system.

Explanation:
ग्रेट रेड स्पॉट बृहस्पति ग्रह पर स्थित एक विशाल तूफान है, जो पृथ्वी से भी बड़ा है। यह एक उच्च दबाव क्षेत्र है जो कम से कम 350 वर्षों से सक्रिय है। इसकी खोज 1664 में रॉबर्ट हुक ने की थी। यह तूफान बृहस्पति के वायुमंडल में अमोनिया और जल के बादलों से बना है। इसका रंग लाल होने का कारण अभी तक पूरी तरह से स्पष्ट नहीं है, लेकिन माना जाता है कि यह सूर्य के प्रकाश के साथ रासायनिक प्रतिक्रियाओं के कारण होता है। बृहस्पति सौर मंडल का सबसे बड़ा ग्रह है और इसे गैस दानव कहा जाता है।

question: South West Monsoon generates in _______A. Arabian SeaB. Pacific OceanC. Bay of BengalD. Himalayas (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: C
B
D
A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Arabian Sea

Explanation:
The South West Monsoon originates in the Arabian Sea. This monsoon is the primary source of rainfall in India. During summer, intense heating of the Indian subcontinent creates a low-pressure area, drawing moisture-laden winds from the Indian Ocean. These winds are known as the South West Monsoon. The branch from the Arabian Sea brings rainfall to the Western Ghats and northwestern India. Another branch comes from the Bay of Bengal and moves northeastwards. Thus, the South West Monsoon originates in the Arabian Sea, not in the Pacific Ocean or Himalayas. The monsoon is crucial for Indian agriculture and economy.

☛ Which region gets rain from Arabian Sea branch? → Western Ghats and Northwestern India
☛ Where does the Bay of Bengal branch go? → Northeastwards
☛ From which language is the word monsoon derived? → Arabic
question_hi: दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून _______ में उत्पन्न होता हैA. अरब सागरB. प्रशांत महासागरC. बंगाल की खाड़ीD. हिमालय (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 1)

B

solution_hi:

Explanation:
दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून अरब सागर में उत्पन्न होता है। यह मानसून भारत में वर्षा का प्रमुख स्रोत है। गर्मियों में भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप के तीव्र तापन के कारण निम्न दबाव का क्षेत्र बनता है, जो हिंद महासागर से नमीयुक्त हवाओं को खींचता है। ये हवाएं दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून के रूप में जानी जाती हैं। अरब सागर से आने वाली धारा पश्चिमी घाट और उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत में वर्षा लाती है। दूसरी धारा बंगाल की खाड़ी से उत्तर-पूर्व की ओर बहती है। इस प्रकार, दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून की उत्पत्ति अरब सागर से होती है, न कि प्रशांत महासागर या हिमालय से।

question: Which state of India produces the highest quantity of Jute?A. BiharB. OdishaC. West BengalD. Jharkhand (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: B
A
C
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is West Bengal

Explanation:
In India, the highest production of jute occurs in the state of West Bengal. It accounts for over 70% of the country's jute output, mainly in the Hooghly River basin. Jute cultivation requires a warm and humid climate, high rainfall, and alluvial soil, all of which are abundant in West Bengal. According to 2018-19 data, West Bengal produced about 1.2 crore bales of jute, which is roughly 50% of India's total production. Other major producers include Bihar, Assam, and Odisha. Jute is used for making sacks, ropes, carpets, and paper.

Explanation:

question: _______ Soil is red in color and not suitable for agriculture found along Tamil Nadu, Odisha, and small parts of Chotanagpur and Meghalaya.A. Alluvial SoilB. Red soilC. Laterite SoilD. Regur Soil (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: A
B
D
C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Laterite Soil

Explanation:
Laterite soil is red in color and found in Tamil Nadu, Odisha, and small parts of Chotanagpur and Meghalaya. This soil is acidic and deficient in nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, making it unsuitable for agriculture. Laterite soil forms in regions with high temperature and heavy rainfall, where leaching is intense. The red color is due to the high content of iron oxide.

☛ Where does laterite soil form? → High temperature and heavy rainfall regions
☛ What gives laterite soil its red color? → High iron oxide content

question: _______ are a mountain range that runs almost parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula, and is one of the eight “hottest hotspots” of biological diversity in the world sometimes called the “Great Escarpment of India”.A. Eastern GhatsB. Western GhatsC. HimalayasD. Satpura Range (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: C
D
A
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Western Ghats

Explanation:
The Western Ghats are a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India. They are also known as the 'Great Escarpment of India'. This range is one of the eight hottest biodiversity hotspots in the world. It is about 1600 km long and extends from Gujarat to Kerala. The Western Ghats contain many national parks and wildlife sanctuaries. Several plants and animals found here are endemic, such as the Nilgiri tahr and Malabar civet. It is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

question_hi: _______ एक पर्वत श्रृंखला है जो भारतीय प्रायद्वीप के पश्चिमी तट के लगभग समानांतर है, और दुनिया में जैविक विविधता के आठ "सबसे प्रसिद्ध हॉटस्पॉट" में से एक है जिसे कभी-कभी "भारत की महान कगार" कहा जाता है।A. पूर्वी घाटB. पश्चिमी घाटC. हिमालयD. सतपुड़ा पर्वत (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)

पश्चिमी घाट एक पर्वत श्रृंखला है जो भारत के पश्चिमी तट के समानांतर चलती है। इसे 'भारत की महान कगार' भी कहा जाता है। यह दुनिया के आठ सबसे महत्वपूर्ण जैव विविधता हॉटस्पॉट में से एक है। इसकी लंबाई लगभग 1600 किलोमीटर है और यह गुजरात से केरल तक फैला है। पश्चिमी घाट में कई राष्ट्रीय उद्यान और वन्यजीव अभयारण्य हैं। यहाँ पाए जाने वाले कई पौधे और जानवर स्थानिक हैं, जैसे कि नीलगिरि तहर और मालाबार सिवेट। यह यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल भी है।

question: The river Godavari does NOT pass through which of the following states?A. MaharashtraB. GujaratC. ChhattisgarhD. Andhra Pradesh (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: A
C
D
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gujarat

Explanation:
The Godavari river flows through the states of Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh, but does not pass through Gujarat. It originates in the Trimbakeshwar hills of the Western Ghats in Maharashtra and empties into the Bay of Bengal. Godavari is the second longest river in India, with a length of about 1465 km. It is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Ganga of the South'. The river flows through Nasik, Aurangabad (Maharashtra), Bastar (Chhattisgarh), Warangal, Khammam (Telangana), and Rajahmundry (Andhra Pradesh). The Godavari basin is the largest in India by area.

question: Due to which of the below mentioned reasons, do clouds float in the sky?A. Low temperatureB. Low speedC. Low pressureD. Low density (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 2)

question: The presence of ozone in the _____ prevents Sun's Harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiations from reaching the Earth’s surface.A. TroposphereB. MesosphereC. StratosphereD. Thermosphere (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: C
B
A
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Stratosphere

Explanation:
The ozone gas is present in the stratosphere, located approximately 15 to 50 km above the Earth's surface. This ozone layer absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, preventing it from reaching the Earth's surface. Thus, the ozone layer protects living organisms from the damaging effects of UV radiation. In the stratosphere, temperature increases with altitude primarily due to the absorption of UV radiation by ozone. Other atmospheric layers like the troposphere, mesosphere, and thermosphere do not contain significant amounts of ozone.

question: Increase in carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is caused by which of the following reasons?I) Excessive use of fossil fuelsII) DeforestationIII) Increased number of vehiclesIV) Excessive use of solar heaters (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: I and II
I, II and IV
I, II and III
I, II, III and IV
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is I, II and III

Explanation:
The increase in carbon dioxide (CO₂) in the atmosphere is primarily due to human activities. Excessive use of fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) releases large amounts of CO₂ when burned. Deforestation reduces the number of trees that absorb CO₂, leading to higher atmospheric CO₂ levels. Increased number of vehicles leads to more burning of petrol and diesel, releasing CO₂. Excessive use of solar heaters uses renewable energy and does not emit CO₂, so it does not contribute to the increase. Therefore, option IV is incorrect.

question: Which of the following is not a greenhouse gas?A.OzoneB. Nitrous oxideC. Water vaporD. Hydrogen (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/03/2016) Shift 3)
options: B
C

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hydrogen

Explanation:
Greenhouse gases are gases that trap heat in the Earth's atmosphere, contributing to the greenhouse effect. Common greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, water vapor, and ozone. Hydrogen (H₂) is not a greenhouse gas because it does not absorb infrared radiation; it disperses quickly and does not trap heat. Ozone (O₃) acts as a greenhouse gas both in the stratosphere and troposphere. Nitrous oxide (N₂O) is a potent greenhouse gas released from agricultural activities. Water vapor (H₂O) is the most abundant greenhouse gas and contributes significantly to the natural greenhouse effect.

question: The largest border of India with which country?A. PakistanB. BangladeshC. ChinaD. Nepal (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/03/2016) Shift 3)
options: C

B
solution:

Explanation:
India's longest international border is with Bangladesh, stretching approximately 4,096.7 km. This border touches five Indian states: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. The India-Bangladesh border includes several enclaves and exclaves, such as Dahagram-Angarpota. In comparison, India's border with China is about 3,488 km, with Pakistan about 3,323 km, and with Nepal about 1,751 km. The border agreement between India and Bangladesh was signed in 1974 and finalized under the Land Boundary Agreement in 2015.

question: In which state did India's White Revolution have its origin? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/01/2021) Shift 2)

Maharashtra
Uttar Pradesh
Odisha
solution:

Explanation:
India's White Revolution, also known as the Dairy Revolution, originated in Anand, Gujarat. It was spearheaded by Dr. Verghese Kurien, known as the 'Milkman of India'. In 1970, he established 'Amul' in Anand and promoted dairy cooperatives to enhance milk production. The revolution was implemented through a program called 'Operation Flood', which transformed India from a milk-deficient nation into the world's largest milk producer. The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), headquartered in Anand, played a pivotal role in replicating the Anand model across the country. The White Revolution not only boosted rural economy but also empowered millions of small farmers.

question: Which strip of water separates India and Sri Lanka? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/01/2021) Shift 2)
